subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is NOT a standard modelling assumption in mechanics?
questions.explain: An object's colour has no mechanical effect and is never a modelling assumption.

questions.q: Resolving a force into components is possible because force is:
questions.explain: Only vectors can be resolved into perpendicular components.

questions.q: A smooth surface in a mechanics model means:
questions.explain: Smooth means frictionless, so no frictional force acts along the surface.

questions.q: The quantity kg m^2 s^-2 corresponds to which physical quantity?
questions.explain: kg m^2 s^-2 is the joule, the unit of energy/work.

questions.q: The assumption that a string is inextensible means:
options: Its length does not change under tension
questions.explain: Inextensible means the string does not stretch, so connected objects share the same acceleration.

questions.q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explain: Distance has magnitude only, making it a scalar; the others are vectors.

questions.q: Which list contains only vector quantities?
questions.explain: Force, velocity and acceleration all have direction, so all three are vectors.

questions.q: The weight of an object acts:
options: Vertically downward through the centre of mass
questions.explain: Weight is the gravitational force acting vertically downward through the centre of mass.

questions.q: The base units of power (the watt) are:
questions.explain: Power = energy/time = kg m^2 s^-2 / s = kg m^2 s^-3.

questions.q: Which equation is dimensionally consistent, where s is distance, u and v speeds, a acceleration, t time?
questions.explain: Each term in s = ut + (1/2)at^2 has units of metres, so it is dimensionally consistent.

questions.q: The accepted approximate value of g used in A-level mechanics is:
questions.explain: Acceleration due to gravity is modelled as 9.8 m s^-2.

questions.q: The SI base units of the joule (energy) are:
questions.explain: Energy = force x distance = (kg m s^-2)(m) = kg m^2 s^-2.

questions.q: The base units of acceleration are:
questions.explain: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity = (m s^-1)/s = m s^-2.

questions.q: Why is treating a car as a particle acceptable when finding its acceleration along a straight road?
options: Its size is irrelevant to its overall motion
questions.explain: For straight-line motion the car's dimensions do not affect the analysis, so a point model suffices.

questions.q: Modelling gravity as constant near the Earth's surface assumes that g:
options: Does not vary over the small heights involved
questions.explain: Over the small heights in these problems g is taken as constant.

questions.q: In mechanics modelling, treating an object as a particle means we:
questions.explain: The particle model concentrates the mass at a point and neglects the body's dimensions.

questions.q: Describing a string as light is the assumption that:
questions.explain: A light string has negligible mass, so the tension is the same throughout.

questions.q: The base units of momentum (mass x velocity) are:
questions.explain: Momentum = mass x velocity = kg x m s^-1 = kg m s^-1.

questions.q: The SI base unit of time is the:
questions.explain: The second is the SI base unit of time.

questions.q: A pulley is often modelled as smooth and light so that:
options: The tension is the same on both sides
questions.explain: A smooth light pulley changes the direction of the string without changing its tension.

questions.q: Expressed in SI base units, the newton is equivalent to:
questions.explain: Force = mass x acceleration, so 1 N = 1 kg x 1 m s^-2 = kg m s^-2.

questions.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explain: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector; the others are scalars.

questions.q: Which of these is an SI base unit?
questions.explain: The kilogram is a base unit; newton, joule and watt are derived units.

questions.q: Pressure is force per unit area. Its SI base units are:
questions.explain: Pressure = (kg m s^-2)/(m^2) = kg m^-1 s^-2.

questions.q: A force of 1 N gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of:
questions.explain: From F = ma, a = F/m = 1/1 = 1 m s^-2.

questions.q: A rigid rod is modelled as:
options: A body that does not bend or change shape
questions.explain: A rigid rod keeps its shape and length, allowing it to transmit pushes, pulls and turning effects.

questions.q: The weight of a 5 kg object (g = 9.8) is:
questions.explain: Weight = mg = 5 x 9.8 = 49 N.

questions.q: For dimensional consistency, the argument of a sine function or any fully reduced ratio inside a formula must be:
questions.explain: Functions like sine require dimensionless arguments.

questions.q: In F = ma with F in newtons and m in kg, the acceleration a must be in:
questions.explain: To give force in newtons (kg m s^-2), acceleration must be in m s^-2.

questions.q: Modelling air resistance as negligible is most reasonable when:
options: The object is light and slow-moving over short distances
questions.explain: For small, slow objects over short ranges, air resistance is small enough to ignore.
